CRO AUDIT & RECOMMENDATIONS

The magnesium journey asks careful buyers to trust it, then gives them reasons not to

We followed a magnesium shopper from the homepage to the magnesium collection to Triple Magnesium Complex, on an iPhone 13 and a 1440px desktop. We compared each page with five magnesium brands, read what magnesium buyers say, and pinned every barrier to the exact spot on the live page.

The core problem

The science is there. The pages won't let the shopper verify it.

Three things a magnesium shopper runs into, measured on the live site on 12 October 2026.

COMPETITOR GAP

3 of 5
Setu, BiOptimizers, Moon Juice

Note on data: this audit uses no GA4 or Shopify analytics. Priority comes from what a shopper sees and how directly it touches trust, price and the decision to buy. Every factual statement is checked against the live pages and logged with its proof in the accompanying ledger.
Who's actually landing here

Four magnesium shoppers the site has to convince

Built from who the pages themselves write to, their FAQs and testimonials, and the ads that send traffic here.

The sleep-struggler

What she needs to see: Proof it works, a realistic idea of how soon, and reassurance she won't come to depend on it.

Arrives from ads asking "Struggling to switch off at night?" and has often tried melatonin or a basic magnesium. The page gives her three timelines and never says non-habit-forming, though Wellbeing's own Sleep Melts ads do.

The label reader

What she needs to see: The elemental dose, the dose of each form, and evidence that matches this capsule.

The page teaches her to avoid oxide, then cites an oxide study; the collection page tells her to check elemental content, then neither page gives it in text. She is the likeliest buyer at ₹1,189 and the easiest to lose.

The woman managing cramps, PMS or PCOS

What she needs to see: Whether it is safe for her and what it can honestly do for her symptom.

The product page FAQ answers "Yes" to PCOS, the description says claims are not for this product, and the kidney and pregnancy guidance sits only on the collection page.

The active recoverer

What she needs to see: Which of the three magnesiums is built for recovery.

The collection tags Triple Magnesium "Cognition & Muscle" and Ultra Strength "Energy, Stress & Sleep", and the product page points to the others in one line with no comparison.

Category research

What magnesium buyers are actually telling us

From magnesium buyer forums and health guides, and from the five competitor pages above.

What makes magnesium buyers hesitate

Speed: many expect it to work like a sleeping pill and judge it after a night or two (1mg; r/insomnia threads).
Form and stomach comfort: forum buyers say some forms give them diarrhoea and that "it must be glycinate".
Label confusion: a capsule labelled "500 mg magnesium glycinate" may hold only 70 to 100 mg of elemental magnesium, so careful buyers look for the elemental figure.
Whether it is the right magnesium at all: buyers compare glycinate, threonate and citrate by goal before choosing.

What competitors use to win the sale

Dose in plain text: 3 of the 5 brands we checked state their magnesium numbers on the page.
Risk reversal: Setu (60 days), BiOptimizers (365 days) and Moon Juice (45 days) offer money-back guarantees.
Subscriptions: 3 of 5 sell magnesium on subscribe and save.
Delivery terms on the product page: 4 of 5.
